transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I know it probably sounds ridiculous for someone who works in construction, but as soon as I know I have to go up high on a building, I get an overwhelming rush of fear the moment I even approach the scaffolding. It's gotten so bad that I just can't seem to face it anymore.
Do you feel this intense fear only when you are in high places or facing heights, and do you avoid those situations because of it?

Yes, it only happens when I'm dealing with heights, like being on the scaffolding or the upper floors of a building. I do everything I can to avoid it, like trading shifts or turning down overtime just to stay on the ground. If I absolutely have to go up, I end up freezing on the ladder, shaking, and feeling completely sick to my stomach.
Do you feel this same intense fear in other situations too, or is it only when you are exposed to heights?

No, it's strictly limited to heights. When I'm on the ground or just doing normal everyday things, I feel completely fine and don't experience any of this panic at all. It only happens when I have to deal with high places like the scaffolding, lifts, or the upper floors of a building.
When you are near heights, do you get physical panic symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, dizziness, or a feeling that you might faint or lose control?

Yes, absolutely. The moment I get near the scaffolding, my heart starts racing, my chest gets incredibly tight, and my legs feel completely wobbly. It's like my body starts freaking out before I even put a foot on the ladder, and if I try to go up, I just freeze and start shaking.
Do you also feel this intense fear or avoidance in any other situations, or is it only when you are exposed to heights?
No, it is definitely just heights. I don't have any issues like this in any other part of my life, only when I have to deal with being up high on the scaffolding or the upper floors at work.
Have you had this fear of heights for at least 6 months, and does it consistently lead you to avoid or endure those situations with intense distress?

Yes, it's been going on for about eleven months now, ever since I was rotated to the high-rise crew. I will do absolutely anything to avoid going up, like trading shifts or turning down overtime, and if I'm forced to, I either freeze on the ladder shaking or just white-knuckle it through while feeling completely sick.
When you are high up, is your fear mainly about the height itself, or are you also afraid of something else happening, like falling, being trapped, or having a panic attack?

It's really about the height itself and the terrifying feeling of falling. Just standing on those open metal planks with nothing solid around me makes me feel like I'm about to slide right off the edge. I'm not worried about being trapped or anything, it's just the sheer fear of falling from up there.
When you are near heights, is the main fear specifically of falling or being harmed because of the height, rather than fear of embarrassment, panic itself, or something else?

Yes, it's definitely the physical danger of falling from that height. Standing on those open metal planks makes me feel like I’m about to slide right off the edge. I'm not worried about embarrassment or the panic itself, I'm just terrified of actually falling.
Do you have this same fear with other things that are high up, like balconies, tall buildings, stairs, or looking out from a window, or is it only at work on scaffolding?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed feeling this way around regular balconies or windows outside of work. It's really just the open scaffolding and lifts on the job site that seem to set me off.
Do you also get this fear when you are in other high places outside of work, like balconies, tall buildings, stairs, or looking out from windows?

I haven't really thought about it or noticed it much outside of work, to be honest. My mind has been so completely consumed by the scaffolding and trying to get through my shifts at the job site that I haven't really paid attention to anything else.

Do you get the same intense fear when you are in other high places outside of work, like balconies, staircases, or looking out from windows? Or is it only the specific scaffolding/lifts at your job site that trigger it?
I haven't really thought about it or encountered those situations much recently. My focus has been entirely on dealing with the scaffolding and lifts at work, so I'm not really sure.

Do you feel the same intense fear in other height situations outside of work, like balconies, staircases, tall buildings, or looking out from windows, or is it only the scaffolding and lifts at your job site?

I'm not entirely sure because I don't really encounter those other high situations very often in my daily life. I've mostly just noticed this intense fear with the scaffolding and lifts at work. Outside of my job, I don't really run into heights like that.

Do you also get this same fear in other height situations outside of work, like balconies, staircases, tall buildings, or looking out from windows, or is it only the scaffolding and lifts at your job site?

Like I said, I haven't really paid attention to or encountered those other situations much in my day-to-day life. For me, the fear is really focused on the open scaffolding and high-rise construction heights at my job.
Do you get the same fear in other height situations outside of work, like balconies, staircases, tall buildings, or looking out from windows, or is it only the scaffolding and lifts at your job site?

I haven't really thought about it or encountered those situations much lately. My focus has been entirely on the terrifying experiences with the scaffolding and lifts at my construction job, so I'm not really sure about other places.

Do you also feel this same intense fear in other height situations outside of work, like balconies, staircases, tall buildings, or looking out from windows, or is it only the scaffolding and lifts at your job site?

Honestly, I don't really encounter those kinds of heights in my normal routine outside of work, so I'm not sure. I don't live or hang out in high-rise buildings, so it's really just the scaffolding and lifts on the job site that I've had to deal with.
Outside of work, if you were on a balcony, staircase, tall building, or looking out from a window, would you feel the same fear of heights and falling?

I'm really not sure because I just don't encounter those kinds of situations in my normal life outside of work. My focus has been entirely on how this fear is affecting my job and my chances of getting a promotion on the construction crew.
